description: Live NYC family intelligence for AI assistants: neighborhoods, schools, admissions, safety, health, family resources, kids' activities, and neighborhood comparisons.

tools.name: search-neighborhoods
tools.description: Search and filter NYC neighborhoods by borough or name. Returns NTA codes, names, boroughs, and centroid coordinates.

tools.name: get-neighborhood
tools.description: Get full details for a single NYC neighborhood including demographics, raw 0-100 scores, location, and a family-readable interpretation (labeled score bands + cached editorial blurbs). Use the nta_code from search-neighborhoods.

tools.name: get-neighborhood-summary
tools.description: Get a decision-ready, family-readable summary of one NYC neighborhood: a one-paragraph fit verdict, labeled score bands (e.g. 'Peace of Mind: strong (78/100)'), and cached editorial blurbs — with raw scores still available, weekday-morning transit minutes to the city's main job centers, and a link to the neighborhood's Motley page. The interpretation-first front door; start here when a family wants an answer, not a data dump. A non-residential area (park, cemetery, airport, institution) isn't scored, and the summary says so.

tools.name: get-schools
tools.description: Get schools within a neighborhood — public, charter, and private. Includes quality ratings, grade levels, contact info. Use count_only for a quick summary, or limit/offset to page the full list (the response reports total/returned).

count_only.description: Return only counts by governance type

limit.description: Max schools to return (ignored when count_only)

offset.description: Number of schools to skip, for paging through the full list

tools.name: browse-schools
tools.description: Find NYC schools citywide by what a family wants — borough, community school district (1-32), grade band (pre-K/elementary/middle/high), school type (public/charter/private), admissions method (zoned, screened, unscreened, limited unscreened, ed-opt, audition, SHSAT, charter lottery, private, universal pre-K), and program focus (arts, sports, STEM, language, academic, clubs). Use this when the family describes the KIND of school they want; use get-schools when you already have an nta_code and want everything in that neighborhood. Pass only the filters actually stated — at least one is required, and an invented one returns nothing. Program focus is tagged on public and charter schools only.

borough.description: Limit to one borough. Omit unless the family named one.

district.description: Community school district numbers, 1-32. A borough is NOT a district — for 'schools in the Bronx' use `borough` and omit this. Never guess one.

grade_band.description: prek (K-12 schools that also run 3-K/pre-K), elementary (K-5), middle (6-8), high (9-12)

governance.description: School type. Omit unless the family named one.

admissions_method.description: How the school admits students; matches a school admitting by ANY listed method. Call get-admissions-methods or explain-admissions-method for what each one means.

program_categories.description: Program focus; matches a school offering ANY listed focus. 'arts' covers art, music, dance, drama and theater; 'extracurricular' means clubs. Tagged on public and charter schools ONLY.

offset.description: Number of schools to skip, for paging

tools.name: find-school
tools.description: Use this to turn a school's name into its DBN — the official name, a common short form ('Brooklyn Tech', 'PS 321'), or a DBN to confirm. Returns candidate schools with their district, neighborhood, admission method and Motley page; pick the one that matches and pass its dbn to get-admissions-demand. Never guess a DBN. K-12 schools only (public, charter, private).

query.description: The school as the family named it: its official name ('Townsend Harris High School'), a common short form ('Brooklyn Tech', 'PS 321'), or its DBN ('02M475').

borough.description: Narrow a name search to one borough when the family named it. Ignored when the query is a DBN.

annotations.title: Look up a school by name

tools.name: get-zoned-school
tools.description: Use this when a family asks which elementary school is zoned for a specific NYC address, such as an apartment or building they name. NYC draws school zones building by building, so pass the street address exactly as they typed it — building number and street, ideally with the borough — never the device's location. Returns the zoned K-5 school, the neighborhood, and how zoned admission works; some areas, like all of District 1, have no zoned school.

address.description: The NYC street address to look up, as the family typed it, with the building number and ideally the borough — e.g. "123 7th Ave, Brooklyn". A zone line can run between two buildings on one block, so a city or neighborhood can't answer this; never the device's location.

annotations.title: Find the zoned school for an address

tools.name: get-resources
tools.description: Get family resource counts for a neighborhood: recreation centers, playgrounds, libraries, hospitals, farmers markets, ADA subway stations.

tools.name: get-activities
tools.description: Get kids' activities and businesses in a neighborhood — classes, sports, arts, tutoring, etc. Use count_only for category breakdown, or limit/offset to page the full list (reports total/returned). Each place's last_refreshed is when we last confirmed it was still listed.

limit.description: Max activities to return (ignored when count_only)

offset.description: Number of activities to skip, for paging through the full list

tools.name: get-safety
tools.description: Get safety and health environment indicators for a neighborhood: crime complaints, collisions, HPD violations, air quality, lead levels, asthma rates — plus a family-readable interpretation of the Peace of Mind and Air & Child Health scores.

tools.name: get-comparable
tools.description: Find neighborhoods most similar to a given one based on a 9-dimension score vector (family density, wealth, education, safety, transit, etc.). Returns similarity scores.

nta_code.description: NTA code to find similar neighborhoods for

tools.name: find-neighborhood
tools.description: Find which NYC neighborhood (NTA) an address or coordinate is in. Pass a NYC address the family gave (placed with NYC's official address directory; include the borough when you know it) OR lat+lng. Returns the NTA code, name, borough, a link to the neighborhood's Motley page, and a decision-ready family-fit summary. Use this to turn a real-world location into a neighborhood you can pass to the other tools.

address.description: A NYC street address or place name the family gave (e.g. "350 5th Ave, Manhattan") — never the device's location. Geocoded with NYC's official address directory; include the borough when you know it. Provide this OR lat+lng.

lat.description: Latitude of a point the family named or picked (NYC box) — never the device's location. Provide with lng instead of an address.

lng.description: Longitude of a point the family named or picked (NYC box) — never the device's location. Provide with lat instead of an address.

tools.name: rank-neighborhoods
tools.description: Rank NYC neighborhoods by what a family cares about. Pass per-metric weights (family density, schools, affordability, neighborhood character, transit, safety, air quality & child health) and/or ranked priority keywords; optionally scope to one borough. Keywords that map to a metric: safety, schools, academics, affordability, budget, transit, commute, walkability, proximity, community. Any other keyword, including diversity and parks, adds no weight, because no neighborhood score measures it. Returns the top neighborhoods with a fit score and the metric breakdown — a deterministic weighted sort over neighborhood-level data, not a per-child school match.

weights.description: Per-metric importance (0+; higher = matters more). Any subset; normalized internally. Overrides priorities when both are given.

priorities.description: Ranked priority keywords, most important first — e.g. ["safety","schools","affordability"]. Mapped to metric weights with rank decay (used only when `weights` is absent).

borough.description: Restrict the ranking to one borough

limit.description: How many top neighborhoods to return

min_population.description: Residential floor — drops parks/cemeteries/airports that score ~100 by having almost no residents (default 1000).

tools.name: compare-neighborhoods
tools.description: Compare 2–6 NYC neighborhoods side by side across the 9 family-fit metrics (Family Fit, Families, Affordability, Schools, Neighborhood Character, Transit, Safety, Health, Activities). Pass an array of NTA codes; returns a per-metric matrix with each neighborhood's band and the per-metric leader, plus weekday-morning transit minutes from each to the city's main job centers. Non-residential areas aren't scored and are dropped.

nta_codes.description: 2–6 NTA codes to compare side by side (from search-neighborhoods). Unknown and unscored codes (non-residential areas) are dropped.

tools.name: explain-score
tools.description: Use this when a family asks how one of Motley's scores is computed — a neighborhood score (Family Fit, Schools, Safety / Peace of Mind, Affordability, Getting Around, Neighborhood Character, Air & Child Health, Things to Do) or the school rating — or whether the scores are biased toward wealthier areas. Returns what the score measures, its inputs and weights, how they combine, its share of Family Fit, its known limits, its sources, and how it moves with neighborhood income (Spearman's ρ with median household income). Relay the income figure plainly; don't reassure past it.

topic.description: The score or topic in the family's words: 'safety', 'family fit', 'school rating', 'schools', 'affordability', 'getting around', 'character', 'air quality', 'things to do' — or 'bias' / 'fairness' for how the scores relate to neighborhood income.

tools.name: find-collections
tools.description: Use this when a family asks for lists of NYC schools or neighborhoods picked by a rule rather than a ranking: zoned schools that beat their district while serving high-need students; high school programs with more seats per applicant; schools where no group is a majority and families rate them highly (kind 'schools'); or affordable family neighborhoods with such a school, and family neighborhoods where no single group is a majority (kind 'neighborhoods'). Optionally one borough. Each list carries its rule, its true count and its first members. State the rule; don't call members 'best' or 'hidden gems'.

kind.description: 'neighborhoods' for the neighborhood lists (affordable family neighborhoods with a school that beats its district; family neighborhoods where no single group is a majority); 'schools' for the school lists (zoned schools that beat their district while serving high-need students; high school programs with more seats per applicant; schools where no group is a majority and families rate them highly).

borough.description: Only when the family named a borough; omit it for citywide.

annotations.title: Lists picked by a stated rule

tools.name: get-admissions-methods
tools.description: Get the full NYC school-admissions reference: every entry point from 3-K and Pre-K through Kindergarten, Gifted & Talented, and the 8 middle/high admission methods (SHSAT, audition, screened, Ed-Opt, limited unscreened, unscreened, zoned, charter lottery) — each with its typical application window. The methods carry a live program count plus a special_badge naming any extra ask beyond the standard application (an audition, a test, an open-house sign-in), null when there is none; optional band/governance filters narrow the count. Knowledge only.

band.description: Filter the MS/HS methods to one grade band

governance.description: Filter the MS/HS program counts to public or charter schools

tools.name: explain-admissions-method
tools.description: Explain one NYC admission entry point or method in full — the plain-English explainer, its typical deadline window, and, when the method asks a family for more than a ranked application, exactly what it requires (audition or portfolio, SHSAT registration, a demonstrated-interest sign-in, a private school's own test/interview track) plus the extra paperwork that comes with it. Pass a method key (shsat, audition, screened, ed_opt, limited_unscreened, unscreened, zoned, charter_lottery, private_admissions, prek_universal) or an early entry point (three-k, pre-k, kindergarten, gifted-talented).

method.description: An admission method key (shsat, audition, screened, ed_opt, limited_unscreened, unscreened, zoned, charter_lottery, private_admissions, prek_universal) OR an early entry point (three-k, pre-k, kindergarten, gifted-talented).

tools.name: get-admissions-demand
tools.description: Use this when a family asks how a specific school admits students or how hard it is to get in. Returns the school's admission method in full (what it asks of a family, and when), its programs with seats and who may apply, and — where NYC MySchools publishes them — seats vs. applicants per program with a competitiveness band that is Motley's own, not a DOE rating. Most middle schools, and all charter and private schools, have no applicant counts. The counts describe the whole applicant pool: never turn them into a family's odds, chance or percentage, even when asked for one. Needs a DBN; resolve a name with find-school first.

dbn.description: School DBN (e.g. 02M475 for Stuyvesant, 13K430 for Brooklyn Tech). Resolve a school's name with find-school first; never guess one.

tools.name: get-admissions-timeline
tools.description: Use this when a family asks what's coming for their child — which NYC school applications (3-K, Pre-K, Kindergarten, Gifted & Talented, middle school, high school) they'll make, and when. Pass each child's current grade, or an age (0–5) for a child not in school yet. Returns every transition in the next two years with the city's published dates where it has announced them, and the typical window where it hasn't. Never present a typical window as a date.

grades.description: Each child's CURRENT grade, as the family said it: 3-K, pre-k, k, 1–12. One entry per child.

ages.description: Ages (0–5) of children not in school yet, when the family gave an age instead of a grade.

annotations.title: What's coming for a child, by grade

resourceTemplates.name: Neighborhood summary
resourceTemplates.description: A decision-ready family-fit summary of one NYC neighborhood (verdict + labeled score bands + cached blurbs + raw scores), addressable by NTA code. Same payload as the get-neighborhood-summary tool.

resourceTemplates.name: Admission method explainer
resourceTemplates.description: One NYC admission entry point or method in full (plain-English explainer + typical deadline window + any special requirements the method adds), addressable by key. Same payload as explain-admissions-method.

prompts.name: compare-neighborhoods-for-young-family
prompts.description: Compare NYC neighborhoods for a young family in a given borough, weighing safety, schools, and family density.

arguments.name: borough
arguments.description: NYC borough to search (Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, Bronx, Staten Island).

arguments.name: child_age
arguments.description: Your child's age in years (optional — helps weight schools vs. playgrounds).

prompts.name: neighborhood-fit-for-toddler
prompts.description: Assess whether one NYC neighborhood is a good fit for a family with a toddler (playgrounds, safety, nearby activities).

arguments.name: nta_code
arguments.description: NTA code of the neighborhood to assess (e.g. BK0101). Completes against the live NTA list.

prompts.name: kindergarten-admissions-timeline
prompts.description: Walk a parent through how NYC admissions works for a given early entry point (defaults to kindergarten) — the process and the typical application window.

arguments.name: entry_point
arguments.description: The entry point to explain (three-k, pre-k, kindergarten, gifted-talented). Defaults to kindergarten.
